filter_note: V1 set (7) + market briefing + AI news; Today window = Tue Nov 24 (after the morning run) – Wed Nov 25 morning PT (items already on the Nov 24 and earlier briefs not re-led)

market_briefing.lede: Vendors started shipping their playbooks inside the AI assistant rather than beside it: MCP servers can now carry skills, long-running tasks and sign-off prompts into Claude, and a cold-email vendor launched its own model to rank prospects before anything is sent.

bullets.text: Nov 24: Skills over MCP (public beta) lets a connected app publish step-by-step skills with its tools; HubSpot uses it to onboard customers in Claude. Tasks (long background jobs; ZoomInfo runs deeper account and contact research) and Elicitation (the server pauses for user sign-off, e.g. before spending money or deleting data) are GA. Enterprise support for skills is "coming soon".

Nov 24: Instantly launched Pulse (PULSE-1), a proprietary sales/GTM model that predicts which prospects will reply before a campaign goes out; Instantly says its top-ranked 20% of leads drew 2.2x the positive replies of an unranked baseline in retrospective testing, with free trials until Dec 1.

biggest_ai_news.title: Anthropic lets MCP servers ship skills and run background tasks in Claude
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 24: Skills over MCP in public beta; Tasks and Elicitation GA; File Uploads coming. Anthropic says MCP has 700M+ monthly SDK downloads and 10,000+ connectors for Claude.

biggest_ai_news.title: Claude artifacts install as Mac and Windows apps
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 24–25: "Install as app" (beta, all plans) gives artifacts their own window, connectors and tiered permissions up to full computer access; off on Enterprise until an owner enables it.

biggest_ai_news.title: OpenAI shows GPT-6 designing proteins
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 24: in lab tests, 35 of 322 GPT-6.2-based minibinder designs bound their targets; OpenAI also added healthcare model configurations to the Responses API.

biggest_ai_news.title: Meta puts Muse in Instagram DMs; Walmart opens checkout to it
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 24: Muse can shop Walmart Black Friday deals and check out after the user signs in and sets an Agent Profile with a spending limit.

what_changed.title: Nooks launches Org Charts and Warm Intros
what_changed.body: Nov 24: part of Nooks Deal Intelligence. Org Charts build the buying committee for one account or a whole book from CRM data and the team's calls, meetings and emails (filled in from LinkedIn and the web), flag people not yet in the CRM or never contacted, and add them to a sequence from the chart. Warm Intros rank paths in through teammate and exec connections, former champions, customer alumni and real work/school overlap, and route the intro ask to the teammate in Slack.

what_changed.title: MCP servers can now carry skills, background tasks and approval prompts into Claude
what_changed.body: Nov 24: Skills over MCP is in public beta (on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra; Team admins opt in; Enterprise coming soon). Tasks and Elicitation are GA for Pro, Max and Ultra and rolling out to Team and Enterprise. HubSpot ships onboarding skills; ZoomInfo uses Tasks for deeper research.

what_changed.title: Instantly launches its own sales model
what_changed.body: Nov 24: Pulse is a proprietary model trained on what Instantly calls billions of sales interactions; it ranks leads by likelihood of a positive reply and powers five new Instantly products.

what_changed.title: OpenAI details how Clay runs on GPT-6
what_changed.body: Nov 24: an OpenAI customer story says Clay uses GPT-6 Sol as its primary model, Astra for harder tasks and Luna for cost-sensitive work, offers Clay plugins in ChatGPT and Codex, and is building inbound sales-development features in which an agent shows a product to a prospect.

what_changed.title: Gong is now available in Korean
what_changed.body: Nov 24: Gong said on LinkedIn that its product is now available in Korean for organizations in Korea, and that more languages are coming.

quiet_note: No launch, funding, M&A or pricing of their own from Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft or Monaco dated Nov 24–25. Salesforce's X posts were Cyber Week customer stories (Nestlé, FIDE, F1); Clay's Nov 24–25 X posts were guides and GTM-engineer content.

market_direction.label: Accelerating (vendor playbooks inside AI assistants)
market_direction.text: Skills over MCP (Nov 24) lets apps like HubSpot ship workflows into Claude, after ChatGPT for Sales plugins from Clay, Outreach and Nooks (Nov 17–19); OpenAI's Clay story (Nov 24) adds a Codex plugin.

market_direction.label: New (vertical models for outbound)
market_direction.text: Instantly's Pulse (Nov 24) ranks prospects with its own model, while Clay routes work across GPT-6 Sol, Astra and Luna by cost (Nov 24).

market_direction.label: Accelerating (buying-committee mapping from activity data)
market_direction.text: Nooks builds org charts and warm-intro paths from calls, emails and CRM history (Nov 24).

market_direction.label: Steady (Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft, Monaco)
market_direction.text: No new announcements of their own Nov 24–25; Gong added Korean (Nov 24).

OpenAI customer story: GPT-6 Sol primary model, plugins in ChatGPT and Codex, inbound SDR demo agent in development (Nov 24).

watch.title: Wed Dec 2: Salesforce Q3 FY27 results
watch.body: Results after the close, call 2:00 PM PT. Salesforce forecast that AI and agents will influence $75.8B of Cyber Week (Nov 24–30) online sales; expect agent-commerce numbers alongside the first quarter of the $50/user Coworker SKU, Copilotforce and Coworker in the SMB suites.

interpretation.fact: Nov 24 Nooks launched Org Charts and Warm Intros; Gong became available in Korean. Nov 24 Anthropic put Skills over MCP in public beta and made Tasks and Elicitation GA (HubSpot, ZoomInfo among users); Claude artifacts became installable as desktop apps (beta). Nov 24 Instantly launched its Pulse sales model; OpenAI published a customer story on Clay's GPT-6 use and ChatGPT/Codex plugins; OpenAI reported GPT-6 protein-design results; Meta put Muse in Instagram DMs with Walmart checkout. Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft and Monaco announced nothing new of their own Nov 24–25.
interpretation.interpretation: With skills shipped by the data vendor itself, the workflow that used to live in a sales tool's UI can now arrive inside the rep's assistant, so differentiation shifts to the data and the playbook rather than the screen. Instantly and Nooks are both betting that proprietary activity data (replies, calls, relationships) is what a general model cannot replicate.

feed.summary: Nooks launched Org Charts, where its deal agents map the whole buying committee, and Warm Intros, which tell reps who on their team can get them an introduction.
Gong is now available in Korean, with more languages coming.
